explanations: record() writes to buckets 0..15 (hash % SALT_BUCKETS), but total() only reads buckets 0..14 because the loop stops at SALT_BUCKETS - 1. Views landing in bucket 15 (about 1/16 of sessions) are never counted, so every video under-reports by roughly 6%.

Redis Cluster hashes only the substring inside {} when present, so all bucket keys of a video share a slot and multi-key commands like MGET/DEL are allowed. Braces have nothing to do with value types or sort order, and the colon-separated prefix already distinguishes videos.

Because every bucket shares one hash tag, they map to one slot and one node; salting splits the single hot key into 16 keys but does not spread load across nodes. It has no effect on replica consistency, and nothing deduplicates viewers: the same session simply increments the same bucket again.

The POST handler catches errors from record(), logs a warning, and still responds 202, so the view is dropped. It does not call next(err), so no 500; the 400 path is only for a missing header; and the catch path responds immediately after the failed call.
